rationale: All 9 prior blocking findings verified resolved in current source: ownership guards added to both GET endpoints (CR-003, CR-004); enum literals replaced with ResourceType/PrincipalType members in both repository query sites (CR-005); grant() and revoke() unified into single-session blocks (CR-006, CR-007); is_shared_with none-id guard present (CR-001); ShareUsersRequest min_length=1 constraint present (CR-002); aquery_active_users gained exclude_user_type used in search_sharable_users (CR-008); migration new_values lowercased to match Python enum (CR-009).

business_review.item: AC#1 — POST /share with user_ids grants READ access; recipient can converse
business_review.notes: grant() writes Permission rows and is_shared_with gains per-user predicate. Conversation runtime owner-context forwarding not visible in diff.

business_review.item: AC#2 — Shared assistant appears in recipient accessible assistant list (VISIBLE_TO_USER scope)
AC#3 — Recipient cannot edit; Ability.can(WRITE) returns False
business_review.notes: Permission rows carry permission_level=READ. Existing WRITE-ability check is unchanged.

business_review.item: AC#4 — DELETE /share revokes access for listed users; subsequent reads return 403
business_review.notes: revoke() deletes Permission rows. Post-revocation 403 depends on is_shared_with returning False; not explicitly tested in new tests.

business_review.item: AC#5 — After revocation assistant no longer appears in revoked users' list
business_review.notes: per_user_grant_condition in list queries uses subquery; once Permission row is deleted the OR arm is false.

business_review.item: AC#6 — GET /sharable-users returns only is_external_user=False and is_active=True users
business_review.notes: aquery_active_users now excludes external users at SQL level via exclude_user_type parameter; Python-level filter removed.

business_review.item: AC#7 — POST/DELETE /share by non-owner returns 403; no Permission row created or deleted
business_review.notes: _require_owner raises 403 before any DB writes; tests cover grant and revoke non-owner paths.

business_review.item: AC#8 — GET /shared-with returns current shared-with list for grant-access view
business_review.notes: Endpoint loads assistant and calls _require_owner before list_shared_with; ownership guard confirmed at router line 3235.

business_review.item: AC#9 — Shared assistant appears in recipient personal project view
business_review.notes: _filter_for_regular_user_visibility non-global branch includes per_user_grant_condition with enum members.

business_review.item: AC#10 — shared:true and per-user grants coexist without conflict
business_review.notes: is_shared_with evaluates project-shared first, then per-user grant; OR semantics in list queries are independent.

business_review.item: AC#11 — Recipient conversation executes against assistant's datasources without error
business_review.notes: Runtime context forwarding not in this diff; requires integration or conversation test evidence.

finding_status.notes: Guard `if not self.id: return False` present at models/assistant.py line 859, before any Permission query.
ShareUsersRequest.user_ids declared `Field(..., min_length=1)` at routers/assistant.py line 145.
get_shared_with loads assistant then calls AssistantShareService._require_owner(user, assistant) at line 3235 before list_shared_with.
get_sharable_users loads assistant then calls AssistantShareService._require_owner(user, assistant) at line 3263 before search_sharable_users.
Both per_user_grant_condition blocks in assistant_repository.py use ResourceType.ASSISTANT and PrincipalType.USER enum members (lines 598-599 and 690-691).
grant() uses session.add(perm) inside outer Session block and session.commit() once after loop; no perm.save() calls remain.
revoke() wraps delete loop in single Session block, uses session.merge then session.delete, commits once at end.
aquery_active_users gained exclude_user_type parameter; search_sharable_users passes config.EXTERNAL_USER_TYPE, eliminating the Python-level filter.
Migration new_values=["datasource", "assistant"] (lowercase) aligns with Python enum values; comment in migration documents canonical case.
